finding_key: packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts::no test covers the pkce challenge flowing from the consumed state into the minted code — the whole protection could be silently disabled and the suite stays green
evidence: Working dir is empty, so I judged from the supplied diff and the full auth.controller.ts. The only place the state's challenge reaches a code is auth.controller.ts `createCode(user.id, state.codeChallenge)`; any test exercising that path would have to build state via the *new* 4-argument `createState(mode, port, nonce, codeChallenge)` signature introduced in this diff, and therefore would appear as an added line in auth.controller.spec.ts — none does. The only challenged-code tests (the added `PKCE binding` describe) call `cliAuthStore.createCode(42, challenge)` directly, bypassing `githubAuthCallback`, and the added nonce-echo test builds state with a nonce only and asserts nothing about the code. github-auth.guard.spec.ts likewise stops at "the challenge is in the store". So dropping `state.codeChallenge` at the call site would leave the suite green: a real coverage gap on a security control, though not a live defect in the shipped code.
